metadata.title: Pets-Driven — desktop pets for Claude Code and Codex CLI
metadata.description: A free Windows desktop pet for developers who run AI coding agents. Claude Code and Codex CLI hooks show whether a run is working, waiting on you, done, or failed.
metadata.ogImageAlt: A Pets-Driven pet on a Windows desktop, showing the status of a running Claude Code agent.

hero.headline: You don't code anymore.
hero.tagline: desktop pets for Claude Code & Codex CLI

features.title: What a pet does for you.
features.lede: A Windows desktop pet for people who run AI coding agents. One pet per project directory, so several agents running at once stay readable at a glance.

agents.title: Claude Code and Codex, readable across the room
agents.body: Install the plugin once and every agent event is forwarded to the pet bound to that project directory — each pet opening the agent you picked for its folder. Working, waiting on your input, finished, failed: each state is its own pose and color, and when a run ends or stalls the pet stops and flags you.
agents.alt: A pet's status card moving through idle, working, waiting, and finished

worktree.title: A branch, a folder, and a pet in one step
worktree.body: Run pdd worktree add feat/login, or type a branch into the pet's own menu: the checkout and the pet standing in it are made together. Delete that pet later and it offers to take the worktree with it.
worktree.alt: Branching a pet's folder from its context menu, and a second pet moving into the new worktree

cli.title: A pdd CLI in the box — and agents that use it
cli.body: Hatch, bind, rename, re-skin, note, and delete pets from the terminal — with the app closed, and with JSON output that pipes straight into a script. The bundled hatch, bring, and carry skills let Claude Code and Codex run it themselves, so every Orca worktree gets a pet without a single click.
cli.alt: Claude Code running the hatch skill, then six pets summoned onto the desktop

alive.title: Alive whether or not you're watching
alive.body: With nothing to do, pets greet each other, chat, give chase, and dance — each in its own personality's voice. Take one out and toss it around, hand it a treat, pet it and get an answer back. Quiet mode settles them when you need to focus.
alive.alt: Pets playing together on their own

play.title: Give them something to play with
play.body: Drop a ball on the desktop and your pets chase it, kick it, and send it rolling. Or turn a run into a hurdle race: every tool call your agent makes drops an obstacle in the pet's lane — watch it clear them on its own, or take the controls mid-round.
play.alt: A pet with a ball, running a course of obstacles

bind.title: Point a pet at whatever you work in
bind.body: Double-click a pet and it starts a session in a terminal for its folder. Or bind it to a window you already have open — click the one you mean and the pet sticks to it, your browser and your editor included. Click the pet to bring that window back to the front.
bind.alt: A pet bound to a terminal window, following it and showing the run's status

petdex.title: Thousands of pets to choose from
petdex.body: Run npx petdex install and the app finds it. Anything in your pet folder shows up during onboarding and pet selection, ready to bind.
petdex.alt: Installing a pet from Petdex and picking it during onboarding

demo.title: See it in action.
demo.body: One pet per project. Soon your desktop will be bustling with them.

cta.title: Choose your starter.
cta.body: Pick one folder. That's your first pet.
